about: The five stops of the boxwork Marswalk, in the order Curiosity reached them. Written by hand from docs/SCIENCE_BRIEF.md. 'rmc' names the Curiosity waypoint used as the stop's position: the rover's recorded position on that sol, not the exact position of the rock. Fields ending in 'Ours' are the team's own reasoning or assumptions, not NASA statements.

stops.name: Altadena
stops.found: Curiosity's first drill sample of the boxwork campaign, taken on 8 June 2025 from the ground just before the ridges. The bedrock here is laced with white calcium sulfate veins.
stops.taskOurs: Photograph and sample several veins along the outcrop, choosing the freshest exposures by eye.

stops.name: Nodule site
stops.found: Pea-sized mineral nodules, imaged on 21 August 2025. They sit on ridge walls and in hollows rather than near the central fractures, which the mission cannot yet explain.
stops.taskOurs: Collect many small nodule samples from a ridge wall, a surface the rover's drill could not address.

stops.name: Panorama viewpoint
stops.summary: The wide view of the boxwork
stops.found: Where Curiosity's mast camera took its panorama of the boxwork on 26 September 2025: low ridges with sandy hollows between them.
stops.taskOurs: Survey the ridge network from above and choose which fracture to follow to the next stop.

stops.name: Monte Grande hollow
stops.summary: Drill site Valle de la Luna
stops.found: Curiosity drilled the block Valle de la Luna in this large hollow in October 2025. NASA reports carbonate minerals in the sample from a hollow.
stops.taskOurs: Dig into the sand of the hollow and sample the bedrock beneath it.
stops.sourceLabel: NASA Curiosity mission blog, sols 4709 to 4715

stops.name: Nevado Sajama ridge
stops.summary: Drill site on the ridge beside the hollow
stops.found: The ridge about 10 m from the hollow drill site and 2 m higher. NASA reports clay minerals in the sample from a ridgetop.
stops.taskOurs: Sample across the contact between ridge and hollow in one visit. The rover needed separate drill campaigns weeks apart.
stops.sourceLabel: NASA Curiosity mission blog, sols 4709 to 4715
